<reason>B won a close, high-quality debate by converting A's coverage metric into a liability and keeping a cleaner distinction between honest public floors and state-extended private bargains. A's fissured-workplace case and the “both impose, so calibrate” turn were strong, but did not neutralize heterogeneity, imputed consent, dual-market leakage, or B's named alternative of general minima plus client liability.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's recasting of extension as imputed consent and industrial regulation (B2.5–B2.6, B4.5–B4.8), which undercut “she is in the room” and made coverage look like exclusion scored as protection.</best_rebuttal>
